commits.message: Pin a definition ending at a list item's lazy header row; Line names headerLine (review)

Markdown ends a list item's paragraph at a lazy table header row, as markdown-it does (rich-unfiled-791c.qabg)

Rich 15 draws "- a\n| x |\n  | - |" as the item "a", then a table headed
"x"; ours folded both lines into the item's paragraph. markdown-it tries a
table at an item's lazy line as a paragraph terminator, needing only the
delimiter row to be held by the item, and never counts the lazy header as
code. A quote's lazy line it never tries, so `headerLine` admits only
lines lazy to items.

Markdown's quoted list item holds a line by its indentation past its own `>`, pinned against Rich (rich-unfiled-791c.yr79) (#450)

* Markdown's quoted list item holds a line by its indentation past its own `>`, pinned against Rich (rich-unfiled-791c.yr79)

"> - # h\n   > z" is the heading item, then "▌ z" in Rich 15: the line's
text is past the item's content column in the source, but not past its own
`>`. #449 (78549e209) already measures it so; these pin the case with no
blank line before the line, both ways round.

* Pin a quote's line one cell short of the item, and why the items are headings (rich-unfiled-791c.yr79)
